new_architecture: transformer: a compact attention encoder over the 18 waveform time samples, benchmarked alongside a physics_residual_mlp that predicts a multiplicative correction to the GEANT4-truth Birks baseline.
finding: Raw ROOT reproduction passed exactly at 640,737 selected B-stave pulses. The direct GEANT4-truth/Birks traditional lookup achieved res68=0.04024; the old empirical power law achieved res68=0.46236. Across the ML/NN panel including ridge, gradient-boosted trees, MLP, 1D-CNN, transformer, and residual MLP, the held-out winner is geant4_birks_lookup with res68=0.04024. The direct Sci_bar truth prior changes the absolute MeV scale relative to the earlier S14g stopping-table anchor, but the ordering is stable: the physics/Birks baseline remains stronger than generic ML on this run-held-out closure task.
hypothesis: A layer-level GEANT4 truth prior is already sufficient to fix most of the charge-to-energy nonlinearity, so remaining held-out error is dominated by real readout effects, saturation, and event topology rather than a lack of flexible regressors. A digitized GEANT4 response with the HRD sampling chain would test this by checking whether the residual MLP gain persists when simulation produces ADC-like waveforms.

next_tickets.title: S27c: digitized gain-transition response closure
next_tickets.body: Build a digitized HRD electronics response on top of hibeam_g4 Sci_bar truth and rerun the S27b Birks, ridge, GBT, MLP, 1D-CNN, transformer, and residual-MLP panel on simulated ADC waveforms before comparing to real held-out runs.
